hooks.text: The whitest world in our solar system is a giant snow machine.
How does a tiny moon create one of Saturn's giant rings?
This frozen ball of ice is actually spraying hot water into space.

title: The Moon That Acts Like a Snow Machine
description: Enceladus is the most reflective body in the Solar System, using its internal ocean to build one of Saturn's rings.

beats.text: The [whitest](/wʈɤtʈɤst/) world in our solar system is a giant snow machine.
beats.visual: Enceladus natural color full disk mosaic, Cassini spacecraft, 2005

beats.text: This moon, Enceladus, is just 500 kilometers across and reflects nearly all sunlight.
beats.visual: close up of Enceladus's bright icy surface, Cassini mission, 2005

beats.text: In 2005, the Cassini spacecraft discovered massive geysers erupting from its south pole.
beats.visual: Enceladus plumes erupting from the south pole, Cassini mission, 2005

beats.text: These jets of water and organic molecules blast through warm fractures nicknamed tiger stripes.
beats.visual: Enceladus tiger stripes fractures close-up, Cassini mission, 2005

beats.text: Tidal flexing from Saturn and the moon Dione melts a global ocean under the ice.
beats.visual: cross-section illustration of Enceladus showing internal ocean and rocky core

beats.text: Most of the erupting water ice falls back to the surface as fresh snow.
beats.visual: artist concept of snow falling on the surface of Enceladus

beats.text: The rest escapes into orbit to supply most of the material in Saturn's E ring.
beats.visual: Enceladus within Saturn's E ring, Cassini mission, 2006

beats.text: This process continually recoats the moon in a fresh layer of blindingly white ice.
beats.visual: Enceladus brilliant white surface detail, Cassini mission, 2005

beats.text: That is why the [whitest](/wʈɤtʈɤst/) world in the solar system is a giant snow machine.
beats.visual: distant view of Enceladus orbiting Saturn, Cassini mission, 2005
